To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
even a personal mobile phone call tone that is not answered can distract the driver and cause increased errors.
even an ignored phone call causes significant distraction whilst driving and that the magnitude of the distraction is related to the usual intention to answer calls whilst driving.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of a call on a driver who does not answer, and suggests that even in this situation, the driver's performance can be significantly impaired.
the influence of a mobile phone on driver error, even when the phone is not answered.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of a mobile call on driving is greater if the driver is normally inclined to answer whilst driving, than if not normally inclined to answer.
a ringing mobile phone can cause significant driving errors even in the context where drivers have no intention of answering their phone.
mobile phones are a hazard when used whilst driving, and that even when ignored the phone can be a hazard.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mere ringing of a mobile phone can cause a significant increase in driving errors even when a driver has decided to ignore the call.
a mobile phone call can distract a driver and cause more infractions even if they do not answer the call.
the mere sound of a mobile phone ringing can cause significant driving errors, and that the effect is greatest for those who normally answer their phone when driving.
The main takeaway from our work is that
even if you don't intend to answer a mobile phone while driving, you are still distracted by the ringing of the phone.
even when you are trying to avoid the temptation of answering your phone whilst driving, you are more likely to be distracted by the ringing of the phone and therefore more likely to make an error.
the effect of a mobile phone call on driving, when not answering, is more than simply a distraction from the road.
